reviews.text: The ultimate wedding of Shane Black’s wily, aesthetically winsome & warm-hearted sides. In a story of discovering you can fight city hall (so to speak), its mantra is etched ON city hall: “He that violates its oath profanes the divinity of faith itself.”
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: It’s a smart lesson hidden within an odd couple murder mystery and one worth remembering regardless of political affiliation, because oppression is oppression and either you’re a Nice Guy or you’re a bootlicker; can’t be both.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Black does some of his best visual work ever in “The Nice Guys.” It may be his masterpiece. He creates a pitch perfect period piece set in 1977 Los Angeles. The composition of every scene offers a reward to eagle-eyed viewers.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: One of the characters is apparently the talented one and the other, the unsuccessful one. However, an alternation will occur.  Consequently, the conjunction of two opposite but complementary male characters is a style of the director.
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: You have these flat-lines in what is largely a very amusing detective story where dead air sort of takes centre stage for a few minutes every so often, in part because there’s not always something else going on in the surrounding atmosphere to distract...
reviews.author: Josh Slater-Williams

reviews.text: [Shane] Black likes his characters and loves the genre and that's enough to make the tribute / pastiche / affection parody work.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: For its furious pace, a couple of terrific set-piece scraps and for the disarming likeability and chemistry of Gosling and Crowe, The Nice Guys ticks every box for an R-rated good time.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: (Crowe and Gosling are brilliant together in something that sends up their tough guy images.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Abundant with the same type of caustic sarcasm that made Black’s “Kiss Kiss Bang Bang” an underappreciated, yet cult favorite, “The Nice Guys” is smarter than it has to be and in retrospect, like all great crime thrillers, it is a relatively simple story.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: ... It’s the rare crowdpleaser that’s also eccentric and a little bit irritable in an endearing sort of way.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a jubilant, gritty, and guilt-free lark. As a critic, it's so satisfying to see a film that serves as both strong filmmaking and popcorn-munching entertainment.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Crowe-Gosling team might stir unhappy memories of what-were-they-thinking? twofers like Pat Morita and Jay Leno (Collision Course), Ted Danson and Howie Mandel (A Fine Mess) or Jeff Bridges and Ryan Reynolds (R.I.P.D.), but they're a dynamic duo.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The plot is cumbersome until it becomes painfully obvious who is behind it all, and then it becomes trite.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Ryan Gosling excels as a feckless and cowardly private investigator in a buddy comedy full of wit and energy.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Ryan Gosling's best performance this year, and Russell Crowe's best work in a long time.
reviews.author: Ian Brill

reviews.text: The Nice Guys loses its way time and again, and generally not in an intriguing manner. The filmmakers rely on too many clichés and shortcuts (psychotic hitmen, quirky thugs and such) and too much pointless, time-wasting violence.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: Funny and even thrilling by times, but its greatest trick is to make you fall on side with these two not-always-so-nice-guys.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The humor rarely flows naturally, instead arriving in the form of squabbling asides, designed specifically to be separate, segregated moments outside of the plot.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: This mostly disappointing effort from Shane Black can be described much like the private dicks of the title-not exactly great, or even good, but ensures you'll at least have a nice time watching it.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: A fantastic throwback to several eras. At its heart it's a classic 1940s film noir...wrapped in the polyester styling of 1970s crime films...contains the fun 1980s buddy-film banter and chemistry...punctuated by the ultra-violence of the 1990s.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: With outrageous situations and sharp dialogue, Shane Black is someone who has perfected the buddy cop formula and in The Nice Guys it's an absolute blast.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Through the writing and direction, Black has taken something familiar and gave it its own identity. We get the best of his cinematic obsessions, ranking in the top tier of his oeuvre.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: This is the kind mismatched buddy action comedy that, every time one does roll around, we collectively say, "Hollywood doesn't make this kind of movie anymore."
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: The excessive police buffoonery flows very well, but without much coherence. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: It's a fun experience.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: No shocker, Shane Black is amazing.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: Who knew Ryan Gosling and Russell Crowe would make such a side-splitting pair?
reviews.author: Laura Bradley

reviews.text: ...nobody else makes films quite like this. They're a joy, and watching The Nice Guys was an absolute pleasure.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: THE NICE GUYS is a crucial reminder that we can do action comedies without constantly winking to the audience. It shows not everyone in this type of film needs to be described as 'a badass' - they can be a f***ing idiot, and that's ok.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Don't even get me started on the plot. Again, my suspicion is that Black and Bagarozzi constructed a convoluted story on purpose...
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Grumpy Gosling and growling Crowe are fun, but they can't save The Nice Guys from feeling shoddy.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: The growing partnership between [Russell] Crowe and [Ryan] Gosling is fun to see develop especially when it begins with repeated punches and a broken arm.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling are Disco -- a comedy coupling I am praying already will totally be back for more.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: It could certainly use a lot of trimming, especially towards the drawn-out third act. The laughs become a bit thinner and the plot a bit of a drag. However, the journey to get there is a delightful - wait for it - romp.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: If Kiss, Kiss, Bang, Bang were a hot, unconventional radio single (think anything off of Carly Rae Jepsen's E-MO-TION) then The Nice Guys is like a really great B-side (think any of E-MO-TION's bonus tracks).
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Sporting dialogue hotter than a recently spent shell casing and comedy slightly less dark than a necrophiliac stand-up comedian's set, The Nice Guys targets a niche audience.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Gosling's never been funnier, Crowe's never suited a role better, and Angourie Rice is a revelation.
reviews.author: David Brake

reviews.text: Action-packed, clever, funny and surprisingly tender at times, it checks all the boxes for not just an excellent buddy comedy, but an excellent movie period.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a refreshing entry to Shane Black's filmography. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Ocadiz

reviews.text: It revels in its setting, both time and place, giving off a cool and easy vibe that fits the material perfectly.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Who says nice guys can't finish first occasionally?
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is an anomaly - it's a summertime actioner starring two hugely popular actors that seems specifically designed for the sensibilities of the over-35 demographic.
reviews.author: Di Golding

reviews.text: With a pairing of the comedic charm from Ryan Gosling and the pure grit of Russell Crowe the Nice Guys are a match...
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams

reviews.text: 'The Nice Guys' turns Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling into a truly memorable odd couple and showcases the best elements of writer and director Shane Black's unique take on action comedies.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: Crowe has always been an underrated comedian and here he is to the manor born with a role that suits his gruff, but warm, persona perfectly, and Gosling nails his role too.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a hilarious breath of fresh air that gives us new perspectives on Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling, but also a new star on the rise in Angourie Rice.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a yet another jewel on the crown of Shane Black's gleaming crown of a career, once again reaffirming himself as one of cinema's darlings.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a fun action-thriller with winning performances from Gosling and Rice. I pray Shane Black continues churning out these hysterical stabs at noir pulp fiction.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: There's no arguing with the pitch-perfect imagery of smog-swathed L.A. in the Seventies, nor with the shaggy-dog-seeming but actually well-structured storytelling. Also, The Nice Guys earns a lot of laughs, which is always, well, nice.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Gosling has never been funnier. His timing is priceless. Great stuff from Crowe.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: A timeless caper that is well paced, greatly detailed, tightly written, and hysterically funny all the through.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: An archivist's dream: an action comedy about film preservation.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: It's ultimately Gosling and Crowe's dynamic that is the strength of the film. "The Nice Guys" is aware of itself; it's silly and occasionally ridiculous, but in all the best ways possible.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Even if you didn't grow up in the '70's, you'll love this retro cop comedy... The music, the clothes, the cars, the hair, the banter... [will] make you want to grab your hair pick and head to the disco.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: While it has its laugh out loud moments, there just isn't enough content to make it worth paying the price of a theater ticket.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: Nice Guys is more than a worthwhile movie going experience.
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: Their failure is admirable in this one sense: they didn't let mastery of conventional cinematic form get in the way of shouty commentary about contemporary class relations.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Such a perfectly enticing mystery detective story. Honestly, this movie has it all.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is less about characterization, and more about letting two actors loose that have clearly found a groove for turning great material into gold
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Replete with nudity and violence, if eccentric crime dramas with a dash of dark comedy are up your street, The Nice Guys is your film.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: It's a wholesome mix of movie genres.
reviews.author: Aakriti Anand

reviews.text: Crowe is better -- and funnier -- than he has been for a long while but Gosling struggles to bring his character (a hard-drinking single father) to life, while Black takes the easy comedy option rather too often. Still, I wouldn't mind a sequel.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: They're flawed but likeable characters, set in an outlandish, ridiculously entertaining story. You've got to see The Nice Guys.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Who would have thought that Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling would have such great comic chemistry?
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: What's memorable about The Nice Guys is the crew of not-so-nice kids: the 12- through 18-year-olds who seem remarkably unbothered when bumping heads with coke-addled pornographers.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a piece of contemporary cinema that encompasses everything I love about where we are. It's self-aware, it's clever and above all else, it accepts the faults of people and uses them to create a story about finding humanity.
reviews.author: Julia Alexander

reviews.text: From its opening shot, The Nice Guys charms with an exuberant commitment to cutting, panning, and switching between perspectives, establishing the pertinent plot with no filler.
reviews.author: Peter Walsh

reviews.text: Gosling does a lot of physical comedy throughout the film, and he's a genius at it. The simple act of busting a glass window with his fist results in a comedy of errors that had me laughing for a solid two minutes
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: There's just as many laughs as there are gunshots and Gosling's slapstick physicality and Crowe's wry dialogue bring some much-needed light to the dark.
reviews.author: Alex Casey

reviews.text: Chances are if you liked Kiss Kiss Bang Bang and similar slacker-neo-noir capers like The Big Lebowski (1998) and 2014's Inherent Vice, you'll be happy with The Nice Guys. Best enjoyed with tongue firmly in cheek.
reviews.author: Sarah Griffin

reviews.text: Take two heavyweight Hollywood stars, cast them in a shaggy-dog story set in Los Angeles circa 1977 and assign a writer-director with a proven flair for madcap action comedy. Voila! It's time to get acquainted with The Nice Guys.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: Amid countless remakes like Vacation and sequels like Neighbors 2, which doggedly push for crude atmospheres, this film creates a world that's pure and naturally absurd.
reviews.author: Sam Watermeier

reviews.text: Ryan Gosling and Russell Crowe are a good match in The Nice Guys. But writer-director Shane Black's screenplay seldom strikes fire.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Major props must go to the film's production team for recreating the sounds & looks of the 1970s with such matter-of-fact precision...Some of the suburban street scenes look so authentic it's as though they were filmed with the aid of a time machine.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The thing that sets this movie apart is the magic that happens between Gosling, Crowe, and Rice.
reviews.author: Rebecca Cusey

reviews.text: With a story of smart dips and dives in bell-bottoms over shag carpet and groovy lava lamps, The Nice Guys is sure to go down in history as sophisticated escapism.
reviews.author: Mike Daringer

reviews.text: An almost perfect attempt to exactly split the difference between Lethal Weapon and The Big Lebowski, except it's not quite as good as either one.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: For a while there, something magical was brewing. In the end, it plays like a particularly raunchy and plot-heavy pilot episode to a '70s-era crime-solving buddy series.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: The plot is as convoluted as a Raymond Chandler novel, but Black and his cast deliver the action with such brio and panache that the film remains hugely entertaining even if, like Gosling's hapless hero, you've barely a clue what is going on.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Outrageously funny from start to finish...The two leads play off each other perfectly.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: A refreshing film due to its excessive violence and hilarious originality. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Shane Black's The Nice Guys is a splendid tribute to mystery films of the 70s, featuring a good dose of black humor and surprisingly great chemistry between leads Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a major blast, Crowe and Gosling having the time of their lives bringing all this madcap, blood-splattered lunacy to life.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Too often, The Nice Guys feels like the Funniest Film of 1994. There are worse things.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: The contrast between Gosling and Crowe's acting styles is the basis for the film's humor. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Even though a disposable film, it is entertaining as pulp fiction.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Shane Black's R-rated, 1970s action-comedy is a welcome throwback.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is the first great comedy of the summer.
reviews.author: Lesley Coffin

reviews.text: Fans of cinema will enjoy all the references while casual movie goers will enjoy the action scenes.. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: Watching Crowe and Gosling-who are admittedly enjoying themselves in their respective roles-is fun, but the road wears thin along the journey...
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: This sordid 1970's fast-talking detective noir is the perfect sandbox for filmmaker Shane Black.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: A perfect mix of Boogie Nights and Inherent Vice, but without being as dense or as acid as the second one. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Anaid Ramírez

reviews.text: The cast, the story and tone make this a film worthwhile. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oswaldo Betancourt Lozano

reviews.text: The film works perfectly due to the laughs, shootings, self awareness and excellent comedic timing, but also the influence of noir cinema and the work of Paul Thomas Anderson. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: The chemistry between Ryan Gosling and Russell Crowe makes the movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jessica Oliva

reviews.text: Like one of those great comedies from the old days. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: A great comedy, very retro. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Shane Black's best film yet. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Uriel Barco

reviews.text: Gosling and Crowe star in a film as fun as it is absurd. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Ortiz

reviews.text: Gosling and Crowe have such great chemistry that the whole film works because of it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: A buddy movie full of nostalgia and a great cast. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: One of the best films of 2016. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Benítez

reviews.text: [The Nice Guys is] propped up by the performances, humour, action, '70s detailing, a soundtrack with retro tracks (by Kool & The Gang and Earth, Wind & Fire, among others) and a cameo by the dishy Matt Bomer.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: An exercise in cynicism and cool. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: Shane Black makes the most of the sparky and believable chemistry between Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling with his old-school, buddy cop movie.
reviews.author: Theresa Smith

reviews.text: A comedy that stands out due to its great dose of cynicism and satire of the Hollywood industry. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: ...a sporadically entertaining, exceedingly well-acted diversion.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: 'The Nice Guys' is anarchic, irreverent, juvenile and sometimes downright uncomfortable, but it's also occasionally hilarious. ... A provocative film that pretends to be more stupid than it is.
reviews.author: Richard James Havis

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling have a wonderful, gruff chemistry here, which is key. If this is the beginning of a Lethal Weapon style franchise for the two actors, count me in.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Cartoon pulp.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: An top notch action comedy that leaves you wanting more. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: The director know that in order to make the movie work, he has to include the spectator on the joke. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling represent polar opposites of movie masculinity. It's one of the reasons why their first film together, Shane Black's knowing comic thriller The Nice Guys, is such a pungent delight.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: 'The Nice Guys' delivers action-packed, retro fun.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: A witty but tough noir thriller that offers a greatest hits compilation of the writer-director's best work to date, as well as something a little bit new.
reviews.author: Rob Carnevale

reviews.text: Not so much a mainstreamed 'Inherent Vice' as a civilian superhero movie for those who think they're too smart or 'adult' for costumed superhero movies.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Full of style and cinema to the top. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Toni Vall

reviews.text: Unapologetic, wonderful, fun, sacastic and lucid. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcos Gandía

reviews.text: "The Nice Guys" turns on the chemistry between Gosling's manic detective and Crowe's tough-but-humorous Healy.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: There is an interesting enough mix of verbal comedy and slapstick to keep most amused some of the time and then, well, there's Ryan who works for so many of us on a different level.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: A comedy of groovy errors
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is smart-dumb fun for grown-ups, a mainstream summer palate-cleanser amidst the glut of Spandex-clad superheroes.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: It isn't always pretty but The Nice Guys is an unashamedly absurd, self-mocking, guilty pleasure of a film.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: These Nice Guys finish last.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: More slapstick than gumshoe, The Nice Guys is at its best when riffing broadly on the chaotic chemistry between its chalk-and-cheese male stars.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: They may sound like an unorthodox pairing given that we're accustomed to seeing them in dramatic roles but the pairing of Crowe and Gosling works well.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Mr Gosling is as new to comedy as Mr Crowe, but embraces it fearlessly in a role that requires little dignity and plenty of pratfalls.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: As buddy movies go, it has enough irreverence and originality never just to seem like a cynical rehash of a kind of film that has been made countless times before.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The movie enjoys all the politically incorrect pleasures of the Seventies with a knowing chuckle.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: Two fun characters played by two great actors with fantastic chemistry together go in search of a movie, and - spoiler! - never quite find it.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: The Nice Guys makes you want to catch hold of the first random stranger unfortunate enough to cross your path and demand that they drop everything and watch it.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: I found it laboured, clumsy and for a film designed to provoke laughs, nastily and unacceptably violent.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Director Shane Black may have surprised with The Long Kiss Goodnight (1996), Kiss Kiss Bang Bang (2005) and the first two Lethal Weapon movies, but his latest is a shadow of past glories.
reviews.author: David Edwards

reviews.text: Writer-director Shane Black returns to the comedy-noir vibe of his 2005 hit Kiss Kiss Bang Bang with this riotously funny thriller set in late-1970s Los Angeles.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: An absolute joy of a film.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: It's all hugely enjoyable, packing punches and more laughs than most straightforward comedies, and a successful return to the neo-noir well after Kiss Kiss, Bang Bang.
reviews.author: Rob Daniel

reviews.text: Its over-exuberance is entirely forgivable.
reviews.author: Jasper Rees

reviews.text: A defiantly old-school action comedy that delivers big where it really counts.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: Riotously entertaining action-comedy that combines old-school detective thrills with laugh-out-loud humour and blackly comic violence.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: There are shades of The Big Lebowski in its narrative, which spins out to outlandish lengths only to culminate in a bit of throwaway irony.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Funny and occasionally pleasingly absurd, there are no nice guys in The Nice Guys, just a couple of endearing losers who will have you in stitches.
reviews.author: Marija Djurovic

reviews.text: While you'll probably laugh at the stars' buddy-movie shenanigans, you'll certainly hate yourself in the morning for it -- even if this director never does.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is on another level altogether-wildly entertaining and frequently hilarious. (Splice Today)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: A fun but admittedly violent comedy that features a truly great standout performance by Ryan Gosling.
reviews.author: John Hanlon

reviews.text: When it comes to buddy/action comedies, director and screenwriter Shane Black knows what he's doing.
reviews.author: Charles Ealy

reviews.text: After a while, when you've given up on laughing out loud, you start smiling for those old-fashioned reasons: you're enjoying the characters and the scrape they find themselves in.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: For a knockabout farce, The Nice Guys scores high on the charts.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: A crime tale that leaves the screwball comedy bruised and bloody with a retro reinvention of sorts.
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: ... a wonderfully loopy buddy comedy ... Black's thing remains shaggy-dog humor mixed with offhand bursts of violence. Crowe and Gosling channel the nitwit camaraderie of Abbott & Costello
reviews.author: Glenn Lovell

reviews.text: Fun, violence, crazyness, awesome production values and a cool main cast. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Arce

reviews.text: Shane Black's crisp dialogue, a gift he uniquely has, is a standout and does a solid job in the directing department and keeps the action moving, but it's a sense of Deja vu
reviews.author: Whitney Scott Bain

reviews.text: The very notion of Healey and March's working relationship is absurd but writer-director Shane Black and co-writer Anthony Bagarozzi construct a script that makes no apologies for its absurd twists and indelicate situations.
reviews.author: David Blaustein

reviews.text: It's such fun watching the pair muddle their way through a labyrinth of bad vibes.
reviews.author: Clem Bastow

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling make a good bottom-feeding team (Gosling especially shows a surprising flair for physical comedy).
reviews.author: Jim Lane

reviews.text: Their slapstick physicality (especially Gosling's) and wry dialogue is worth a laugh, but is that due to the script or because it's two serious stars being funny? I think it's more the latter.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: What may be surprising- -- or not -- is the camaraderie between Ryan Gosling and Russell Crowe. Their comedy is akin to Two Stooges.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: Writer/director Shane Black is back with another Private Eye flick and this is a good one...overcoming a byzantine plot that never really does make any sense with a witty script, fine acting and directing, and terrific cinematography .
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: They aren't cops, they're just scumbags of slightly different shades. But the odd-couple dynamic is straight out of the Lethal Weapon playbook and it still works a charm.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: Gosling and Crowe are great in a movie that is only good.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Now, I'm not saying every gumshoe yarn needs physical comedy, but The Nice Guys makes joyous use of the stuff.
reviews.author: Alynda Wheat

reviews.text: A gritty, cynical, hilarious, and mostly satisfying bit of L.A. noir, Shane Black's The Nice Guys sees the bad boy writer-director make a slick return to his signature brand of buddy action comedy.
reviews.author: Gary Dowell

reviews.text: Makes concessions to nothing and nobody - it is about as pure an expression of the writer/director's sensibilities as you could ask for.
reviews.author: Dominic Corry

reviews.text: Quick on its wits and fast with its fists, this is Black firmly back doing what he does best. And nobody out there does it better.
reviews.author: James White

reviews.text: Shane Black's passion can never quite be contained within the boundaries of good taste and I love that about him.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The jokes are funny, but consequences still feel real, and that gives the story a level of depth hard to achieve in screwball comedies of this ilk.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: A cool little neo-noir gem.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Rude, raunchy, violent and very funny action-comedy-mystery with two great leads and a surprisingly terrific newcomer. All in all, I'd call it good unwholesome fun.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: Meekly mustachioed Ryan Gosling and a Russell Crowe slowly morphing into John Goodman make consistently amusing anti-buddies.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: The best comedy of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: [Shane] Black's weakest effort in an age, a shoot-from-the-hip P.I. comedy that isn't half as interesting as "Inherent Vice" and barely as funny.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Black has a potent weapon in Gosling, who's at his zaniest here, his moist eyes and drooping moustache evoking the 1990s Nicolas Cage.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is very much in the Kiss Kiss Bang Bang vein - part thriller, part spoof. And Crowe and Gosling turn out to be very funny, embellishing their performances with some noteworthy '70s fashion items.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a madcap ride with some bumps along the way but there is beauty in the chaos.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: While The Nice Guys is definitely a popcorn movie front-loaded with cracking comic interplay and surreal set-piece action sequences, the package as a whole packs a pulpy punch that cannot be denied.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Most of the laughs are solid and the underlying tone of the film is pitched in such a way that it doesn't undermine our inherent investment in the mystery or the appeal of the characters
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a blast...
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: In a competition between Shane Black first directorial effort and his third, The Nice Guys finishes second.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Sliding into theaters between 'Captain America: Civil War' and 'X-Men: Apocalypse', its busted-out protagonists are a long way from spandex-land. This works to its advantage; 'The Nice Guys' is a goof and a treat, but it's also a breath of fresh air.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: If you like your films to zig-zag for entertainment, this is an always engaging and edgy work, carrying Black's signature elements of conflicting textures which created the sardonic action buddy comedy franchise, Lethal Weapon
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: The tone is offbeat, the juxtaposition of ideas occasionally inspires and goofy moments entertain; yet overall the film never quite satisfies or rises to the level to which it aspires
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: Black layers in devilish sight gag after sight gag with smooth pulpy nuance, while maintaining the requisite forward motion.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Shane Black's The Nice Guys isn't terrible -- it just ducks mediocrity -- but every advance it takes toward quality is made on the strengths of Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is just pure wackiness all the way through - a straight-up crime mystery filled with hilarious antics and plenty of violence. A perfect addition to the summer movie roster.
reviews.author: Kit Bowen

reviews.text: Gosling makes an excellent alcoholic fall guy, Crowe, although quite a tub nowadays, is as enthusiastic a thumper as ever.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: For those attuned to its amiably sleazy vibe and sudden alternations between violence and slapstick, it offers a guiltily pleasurable way to pass an evening.
reviews.author: Christopher Orr

reviews.text: With its sloppy plot, fair to middling acting, and a cheesy look of the seventies "The Nice Guys" is not a nice movie.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Black strips the "Lethal Weapon" formula down to its undies and redresses it with moxie and snark.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Gosling has a knack for physical comedy and self-deprecation that gleefully subverts a decade-plus of rom-coms and Nicolas Winding Refn movies.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Shane Black's best work yet... a smart, funny, sexy action movie... You can tell Black would be happy making films like this for the rest of his life -- and we should be so luck.
reviews.author: Mark Hughes

reviews.text: An invigorating sense of style and attitude, combined with a witty script and charismatic performances, give a considerable boost to what could have been a pedestrian noir thriller.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: ...at once very violent, very funny, and a true original.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: a nail-bitingly suspenseful, wickedly funny, and decidedly hard-boiled neo-Noir pitting nihilism against idealism during the candy-colored decadence of 1977 Los Angeles.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: A wildly entertaining albeit convoluted dark comedy with witty, funny and crackling dialogue and palpable chemistry Crowe and Gosling.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Shane Black re-writes the buddy movie template and gives Crowe a second chance and a franchise. Lots of nasty, unrepentant violence and hookers. Pure enjoyment.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is like James Ellroy by way of Abbott & Costello. Frequently hilarious, often surprising, and consistently fun.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: ... with a winning starring duo and an expertise in grimy, twisty crime stories, Black has made a film that uses its route structure to its advantage to deliver a taste of delicious pulp fiction.
reviews.author: Michael Fairbanks

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is an entertainingly breezy buddy-detective romp that steadfast Shane Black fans ought to get additional mileage from.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: "There are never really any new toys in Shane Black's sandbox but he always plays with them better than the other kids."
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The Nice Guys has a nice feel: just slick enough to keep from falling apart, just brutal enough to keep from seeming inconsequential.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: In the era of comic book superhero over-saturation, Hollywood can certainly stand the originality
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: The New Guys is fast, violent, and doesn't feel like it came out of the summer-movie food processor.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is a strange combination of what Sean Black does best, but his neo-noir feels awkward mixed with buddy cop.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: A heckuva entertaining film.
reviews.author: Gary Rotstein

reviews.text: [Shane Black] never lets the film breathe, and The Nice Guys gets smothered by its own smugness.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Why see this film? Partly because of the leading men, but mainly because of a girl.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Director and co-writer Shane Black (the grand "Kiss Kiss Bang Bang") offers up '70s-era laughs by the guffaw-full, including one great bit in which Gosling borrows heavily from the very late and ever-great Lou Costello.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: You need to see The Nice Guys for, hands down, the greatest comedic performance of the year. It belongs to Ryan Gosling.
reviews.author: Christopher Campbell

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling have mismatched-buddy chemistry to burn. Black riffs on LA Confidential, 48HRs and his own Lethal Weapon script.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: You may not recognize Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling in Nice Guys. Here's why that's a good thing.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Freewheeling buddy comedy has lots of mature content.
reviews.author: S. Jhoanna Robledo

reviews.text: A nice summer treat.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Despite its plot's mechanical issues, The Nice Guys has all the makings of must-see DVD and Blu-ray, when its long-winded story can be offset by the ability to rewind and rewatch some truly funny moments.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: A throwback to an earlier era, when big movies could still have strange little touches and lots of edge.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: It has the byzantine plot of an L.A. noir, but races through it with the breathless energy of Black's other work.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: Few genres are more fun than a buddy movie done right. Crowe and Gosling have a blast with these characters and you get to share in the fun.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: I'd say they don't make them like this anymore, but they just did.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: The brilliantly conceived L.A. auto show climax is like a Rube Goldberg action piece.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: You won't see Captain America and Iron Man squaring off at an airport, but you do get Russell Crowe breaking Ryan Gosling's arm and then cheerfully downing a Yoo-hoo.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: These are smart comedic performances, which more than compensates for the feeling that the pairing is ordinary.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The plot doesn't and doesn't have to make much sense, as the whole point is just to watch Gosling and Crowe tool around a long-lost L.A. in a convertible, trade quips and insults, and occasionally shoot people.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: The biggest problem with "The Nice Guys" is that it can't decide what it wants to be when it grows up --- a comedy or a violent thriller?
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling do exhibit an on-screen chemistry, but I would like to see them together in a better film.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Something of a hip, sexy, violent homage to the comedy stylings of Abbott and Costello, with the roles reversed.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling haven't been this engaging or energised on screen in years.
reviews.author: Philip Concannon

reviews.text: The most fun consenting adults can legally have in a movie theater this summer.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Might go down as the biggest missed opportunity of the summer.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: If you enjoyed the banter, stylings, and male bonding chemistry of a bygone era in the first "Lethal Weapon" flick, you'll probably have the same reaction to this. (Full Content Review for Parents - Sex, Nudity, Violence, Profanity etc. - Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: It's not an especially successful film, but here's a handy tip: if you're not laughing within the first ten minutes, there's no reason to hang around for the remaining 100.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Of all the year's movies that are not "Deadpool," The Nice Guys might be the funniest. Well, it's one of them.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: It's all delightfully fizzy, bloody fun - even if there's the teeniest, tiniest hint of sequel ambitions.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: "The Nice Guys" flies high on the chemistry between Gosling and Crowe, and Black gives them plenty to chew on. It's a gourmet summer treat. Nice, guys.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The film is at its best when Crowe and Gosling are on screen together. They create movie magic; their collective charisma explodes off the screen.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The film works because it swerves and slips and slides around itself with a sort of thrilling abandon.
reviews.author: Alicia Lutes

reviews.text: As an alternative for grown-ups looking to avoid the sequels and general noise of summer, The Nice Guys won't finish last. But it could have -- and should have -- been so much more.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: It's a testament to [Black's] confidence as a filmmaker that such odd touches fit seamlessly into this crazy, nimble detective yarn.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The mix of wit, slapstick, and mayhem has some dead-on period detail and some shrewd commentary on contemporary issues.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Shane Black is back doing the thing he does better than anyone else, writing and directing deliriously entertaining action comedies about mismatched partners battling an escalating threat.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: This movie starts at full speed and never stops. While there are flaws, watching these actors let loose amid a collage of explosions, gunfire, drugs and filth is just too fun to slight Black for some clichés.
reviews.author: AP Kryza

reviews.text: Shane Black's The Nice Guys brings us a 1970s that's halfway between Inherent Vice and the Beastie Boys' Sabotage video, shabby and scrappy and loose.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The Nice Guys makes up for weak characters by consistently subverting the cliches of action movie filmmaking.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: Some viewers may find the violence a bit much, although it does lean toward the cartoonish... Best of all, it's funny. It's fair to say that in this instance, Nice Guys do finish first.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: It creates great on-screen chemistry between Gosling and Crowe - as brute adversaries who partner up as private eyes to solve a criminal conspiracy. And it blows your mind with its sense of absurdity - even while making the crime caper count.
reviews.author: Bruce Kirkland

reviews.text: Because this is set in Los Angeles in the 1970s, we're supposed to think back to Chinatown and The Long Goodbye and excuse the opaque plot, around which Black's eccentric gags float like seasoned croutons in bland soup.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: The nefarious plot at the core of "The Nice Guys" doesn't hold up to the most casual scrutiny. Fortunately, about everything else does in this entertaining crime comedy, from the look to the tone to the throwaway details.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: For a movie predicated on slapstick forward momentum, we spend an awful lot of time driving backward.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Though the plot here may be a confusing, multi-threaded mess ... it's occasionally offset by the exuberance with which Black blends splatter and slapstick, and the leeway he grants his two very game leads.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: It freshens the odd-couple formula with some nice period and father-daughter twists.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: Plenty of general-interest slapstick, wordplay, and buffoonery, adding up to a loopy, well-assembled lark.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Everything has its own illogic in "The Nice Guys," a consistently entertaining, frequently violent and generally slapdash action comedy directed by Shane Black.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Gosling and Crowe do have chemistry, and an obvious sense of humor which gets them far. They'd have gotten farther, though, if the movie, while at times hilarious, didn't have such an uneven feel.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: The concept is solid and Black's formula for this kind of film has worked before. Where The Good Guys goes astray is in Black's decision to downplay the '70s as fodder for his script and the casting of Gosling as the quirky private detective.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling are having some career fun here. It's just contagious enough if you don't expect too much more than that.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: The best thing The Nice Guys has going for it are two laid-back, easygoing, deeply likable performances by its stars.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: Although it hits all of the usual beats of a Shane Black feature, The Nice Guys does so with such remarkable efficiency, brimming with witty banter, solid action and even a little heart, that it feels totally fresh.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: Until going off the rails, The Nice Guys is a locomotive breath of retro air, an action comedy winking while wallowing in slapstick brutality. Punchlines that are actual punches, bones broken funny, that sort of thing.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: While the characters are distinctive and charming, and the dialogue is often pretty funny, The Nice Guys is a large step down on the ambition scale from Kiss Kiss.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: The sheer chaos of it all is exactly what makes "The Nice Guys" such a fun ride.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Strong physical comedy, great timing, winning dialogue and off-the-charts chemistry all make The Nice Guys a hilarious ride.
reviews.author: Lauren Chval

reviews.text: Perhaps unfocused and off-balance at times, but conveying a sense of buoyancy that's as cheerfully contagious as it is freewheeling.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Does it include scenes that some may find painful to watch? You bet. Will you be entertained? Thoroughly.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: A juicy, slam-bang action-comedy cocktail punched up, pimped out and powered down with rowdy, new-fangled film-noir fun.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Absolutely the most fun you'll have in a movie theater this summer.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The Nice Guys borrows from noir traditions and pulp fiction, throwing a fresh coat of smart-alecky comedy over the whole thing.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: There's no reason why it shouldn't be both great fun and warmly human, but alas, it just isn't either.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is more than a nice time at the movies. It's a total delight.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: It all adds up to The Nice Guys being cool, man, very cool.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling save the day. They both look like hell for most of the film, with neither actor demonstrating a wisp of vanity as they throw themselves into this cheerfully nasty mess.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Laughter trumps logic here, and the laughs flow freely.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: The porn, the drugs, the smog, the bad haircuts - you can play it for laughs or play it straight. With terrific performances from Ryan Gosling and Russell Crowe, Black does a little of both.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The film overflows with quips, irony, and physical gags while at the same time relating a noir-tinged story of seedy corruption set in the neon-saturated underbelly of the 1977 Los Angeles porn industry.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: A likably tetchy comedy squinting its way through the chest cough of Los Angeles smog circa 1977.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: The Nice Guys may not be Chinatown, but it could be an updated Lethal Weapon.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling make for a great comedy duo in this dark, cynical noir with an unexpectedly earnest center.
reviews.author: Rebecca Pahle

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling are fine, but they never form a genuine rapport. These actors are known for intensity and screen-hogging, not warmth or comedic timing, and here they seem to be moving in parallel but not fully in sync.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: An affectionate parody of the sort of mismatched-buddy action comedies that proliferated in the seventies and eighties, better than most of them were.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: This run-down, wood-paneled world of AMC Pacers and The Pina Colada Song makes an appropriate setting for this lightweight yet diverting action comedy that, aside from being too long, has the sense not to take itself too seriously.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Even nostalgic nonsense requires more than attitude and energy, which is all that Mr. Black has to offer. And despite all its restless detective work, "The Nice Guys" is unable to track down a soul or a reason for being.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: The Nice Guys never lives up to the promise of its hilarious first 10 minutes, but Crowe and Gosling are good enough to leave you hoping for a sequel.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: The pair bounce so successfully off one another that this feels like a double act for the ages, in a film that actually deserves to spawn a sequel.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Is it fun? Parts, yes, and many will get exactly what they wanted from "The Nice Guys": violence, wisecracks, a couple of choice sight gags ... plus the usual angry-mismatched-buddy-cops-but-not-really-cops routine.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: "The Nice Guys" is basically "Chinatown" remade by Quentin Tarantino and starring foulmouthed, updated versions of Abbott and Costello, as played by two of the most recognizable male stars of our time. Make your purchasing decisions accordingly.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: It's a bombardment of audacity and outrageous humor that never lets up.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is another sub-mental movie for morons churned out by the kind of sophomoric Hollywood machine that trademarks the works of Judd Apatow & Co.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is funny enough when it sticks to its heroes-whether pinned in a tight spot or bickering with each other-that its less-than-compelling intrigues and digressions come as an acceptable trade-off.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: It nicely captures the seediness of L.A. in the '70s , but, despite a very encouraging first act, it loses steam and gets bogged down in its own narrative.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: Consistently funny from beginning to end, even as the story eventually runs out of steam.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: This one's a cheerfully violent blast to the past that's as comfy as a broken in go-go boot.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Surprisingly, as a character piece observing two loners who just might be made for each other, The Nice Guys shines far brighter than expected.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Gosling and Crowe give very charming, lighter-than-air performances.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Boisterous and bombastic without sacrificing the dark cynicism at its heart, The Nice Guys is a violent, propulsive, and knowingly trashy caper that puts a premium on hell-for-leather, hard-hitting entertainment value.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: Russell Crowe and Ryan Gosling are clearly enjoying the hell out of each other in this crime caper set in 1977 Los Angeles. So how can you resist?
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling are a perfect mismatch. They skulk around Los Angeles like a bear and a weasel who just escaped from the circus.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: One of the purest expressions of Black's aesthetic, a bloody, hilarious, convoluted mystery that's as funny as it's dark.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Playing like a spiritual sibling to Kiss Kiss Bang Bang, The Nice Guys is laud-out-loud funny and edge-of-your-seat exciting.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The movie is a throwback in many ways but also proves a dynamic duo can still be just as effective in modern cinema as a superhero ensemble cast. For The Nice Guys, it takes two to make it outta sight.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: [Crowe and Gosling] become a surprisingly brilliant comedy duo, carrying "The Nice Guys" past a few flat jokes, needed edits and a cluttered finale.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: An energetically acerbic, sneakily touching joyride through a bygone vision of Hollywood.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: Glorious mayhem reigns left, right and centre in one of the best - and certainly funniest - films of 2016 to date.
reviews.author: Matthew Anderson

reviews.text: It's overlong by about 15 minutes and goes in too many directions at once. But thanks to a groovy period vibe and the A-list stars, you're along for the ride.
reviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz

reviews.text: Shane Black's The Nice Guys doesn't want for great exchanges, and even disposable conversations brim with acidic wit.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: The duo's swearier Abbott and Costello routine is an endless riot, fueled mainly by Gosling's full-bodied nervy cowardice. His high-pitched girlish scream is ever so beautiful.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: The Nice Guys, ultimately, might be a little too nice, but Black and his cast really want you to have a ball.
reviews.author: Alan Scherstuhl

reviews.text: Gosling does enough stumbling and bumbling and falling from balconies (twice!) to earn the term Keatonesque.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Basically, it's Inherent Vice without the highbrow aspirations, or The Big Lebowski with two Dudes.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: In Gosling's pairing with the laconic Crowe, it finds a genuinely pleasurable pair of losers trying hard to eke out a win.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Watching it you can picture its makers agonizing over the script's every inch: making sure each quip was jot-down-able, each plot turn surprising, each plant given a showstopping payoff.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: The Nice Guys spends two hours treating Crowe and Gosling like a pair of piñatas, beating them mercilessly and unapologetically, and it's watching them crawl out from underneath and towards some form of redemption that makes the film a genuine smash.
reviews.author: Michael Roffman

reviews.text: Shane Black's 'The Nice Guys' is exactly the movie you wanted it to be.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Crowe and Gosling nail it and make this one of the year's most air-punchingly enjoyable movies.
reviews.author: Simon Thompson

reviews.text: The detective genre has persisted because it has everything you could want from a film - intrigue, action, suspense, romance, adventure and humanity - and Black's latest delivers all of that.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: This feels like a movie I should already be referencing as an example of the type of movie that studios don't make anymore, but I can't because it's new.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Subversively skewed, this fast-paced action/comedy is filled with unpredictable chaos and wickedly clever confusion.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: maintains a breezy appeal despite its mishmash of tones. Black's vision of burnt-out SoCal crisis isn't about the issues themselves but the flawed people grappling with them.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: There's little else quite like this fast-paced, deeply funny mystery - except Shane Black's other films
reviews.author: Russ Fischer

reviews.text: Gosling and Crowe's breezy give-and-take goes a long way in elevating "The Nice Guys" above the moments where cynicism overwhelms the comedy.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: The Nice Guys is the perfect, incredibly crafted yet laid-back procedural we've been starved for.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Shane Black, the buddy action auteur, is back in his wheelhouse-and he's delivered another inspired onscreen pairing in the blundering one-two punch of Gosling and Crowe.
reviews.author: Jen Yamato

reviews.text: Based strictly on performance and a cinematic confidence that borders on arrogance, this is a highly entertaining film...
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Ryan Gosling and Russell Crowe, paired up as a goofball detective and hit man, stumble and bicker their way through the funniest roles of their careers.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: The BFG feels very much like Spielberg's Powell and Pressburger film - it's a picture that could have only been made now, but feels rooted in the past.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: An innocent pleasure.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: That the film mostly falls flat has far more to do with the largely unconvincing material rather than with the co-stars, who are more than game ...
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: While their one-liners could be a lot sharper, Crowe and Gosling more than get by on stumblebum amiability.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: The sort of cheerfully hostile buddy bash that's been a staple since the '80s, only this one is singularly clever about its own triviality, and it offers the scruffy pleasure of seeing two great actors dial down their gravitas with style.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

synopsis: Holland March (Ryan Gosling) is a down-on-his-luck private eye in 1977 Los Angeles. Jackson Healy (Russell Crowe) is a hired enforcer who hurts people for a living. Fate turns them into unlikely partners after a young woman named Amelia (Margaret Qualley) mysteriously disappears. Healy and March soon learn the hard way that some dangerous people are also looking for Amelia. Their investigation takes them to dark places as anyone else who gets involved in the case seems to wind up dead.
